name: Pizza DeFi
rootCause: At 8 pm on December 8, the hacker account itsspiderman used an overflow vulnerability to issue additional tripool market-making certificates in eCurve out of thin air, pledged and loaned most of the tokens in the agreement in PIZZA. Afterwards, hackers created more than 1.3 million accounts and dispersed the stolen assets. The loss of the PIZZA protocol in this attack is equivalent to about 5 million U.S. dollars. After negotiations, the hackers agreed to a ransom of $500,000.

descriptions.text: At 8 pm on December 8, the hacker account itsspiderman used an overflow vulnerability to issue additional tripool market-making certificates in eCurve out of thin air, pledged and loaned most of the tokens in the agreement in PIZZA. Afterwards, hackers created more than 1.3 million accounts and dispersed the stolen assets. The loss of the PIZZA protocol in this attack is equivalent to about 5 million U.S. dollars. After negotiations, the hackers agreed to a ransom of $500,000.

On December 8, 2021, the EOS-based Pizza DeFi platform suffered a loss of approximately $5 million after an attacker exploited a vulnerability in the eCurve contract to mint unlimited Tripool tokens. The attacker deposited these inflated LP tokens as collateral on Pizza DeFi and drained protocol assets. Most funds were later returned following negotiation and a $500,000 bounty payment. The root cause was a missing positive-balance check in the eCurve contract on EOS. This allowed the attacker to mint an arbitrary amount of Tripool (LP) tokens, which were then accepted as valid collateral by Pizza DeFi, enabling over-collateralized borrowing and asset extraction.
